evals.prompt: I need a soft power switch for a board running off a single 18650. A momentary button should turn on a 3.3V buck (TLV62569), and the ESP32-S3 should hold it on and read the button to shut down. Pick the parts and write the Stackup KDL for it.
evals.expected_output: DC bias table across 3.0-4.5V with worst-case FET thresholds, a defined rest state for the buck EN pin, button sense kept within the MCU rail, parts with manufacturer/MPN/LCSC and JLCPCB tier, KDL placements and circuits, and a SPICE harness covering insertion, press at low battery, and shutdown.
assertions: Shows node voltages for the latch/EN/sense nodes at the low end (3.0 V) and high end (4.2 or 4.5 V) of the supply
Checks the latch FET against its maximum (worst-case) Vgs(th), not typical
Gives the buck EN pin a defined rest state (explicit pull-down or equivalent) when the switch is off
Keeps the button-sense GPIO within the ESP32-S3's 3.3 V rail in every supply state (no pull-up to VSYS/battery)
Chooses ESP32-S3 GPIOs that avoid strapping, flash/PSRAM and USB pins, or explicitly justifies any exception
Every placement in the KDL has manufacturer and MPN
Reports JLCPCB library tier (Basic/Extended) and stock for the chosen parts
Ran stackup check on the design and it reports 0 errors
Ran a SPICE simulation covering at least battery insertion and a button press at the lowest supply
Cites manufacturer datasheets (table/section) for the thresholds used

evals.prompt: can you swap the 2N7002 on the latch gate for something with a lower threshold? keep it SOT-23 and cheap at jlc
evals.expected_output: Candidates checked by max Vgs(th) against the actual gate drive at the lowest supply, pinout compatibility confirmed from datasheets, JLCPCB tier and stock plus a second source, the KDL placement updated with manufacturer/MPN/LCSC, and a reminder to rerun stackup check, sync the PCB and rerun the latch simulation.
assertions: States the replacement FET's maximum Vgs(th) and shows it is below the actual gate drive at the lowest supply with margin
Computes the gate drive using the real diode drop / divider at the lowest supply (about 3.0 V)
Checks the off/insertion case: a lower-threshold FET must still stay off (gate below its minimum Vgs(th))
Confirms the SOT-23 pinout (G/S/D) matches the 2N7002 from the manufacturer datasheet
Reports JLCPCB tier (prefers Basic) and stock for the chosen part
Names at least one second source or alternative part
Updates the placement with manufacturer, MPN and LCSC fields
Ran stackup check on the edited design and it reports 0 errors
Tells the user the follow-up steps: sync the PCB and re-run the latch simulation

evals.prompt: We're about to send this board to the fab for assembly. What do I need to check and export first?
evals.expected_output: A pre-order checklist: stackup check --locked, PCB in sync with Stackup, DRC clean with documented exceptions, unambiguous BOM (LCSC numbers for JLCPCB or stackup bom CSV with MPN columns), footprints vs package drawings, polarity/rotation review, production files regenerated, and the bench checklist.
assertions: Includes running stackup check (ideally --locked)
Includes confirming the KiCad PCB is in sync with the Stackup design
Includes DRC with zero errors and documented exceptions
Requires every BOM line to have MPN, manufacturer, value, package and description
Notes that stackup bom has no package/description columns, or otherwise explains how package/description reach the fab
Covers LCSC numbers for JLCPCB assembly or MPN columns for other assemblers
Includes checking footprint geometry against manufacturer package drawings
Includes reviewing polarity/rotation in the assembler's placement preview
Includes re-checking stock at order time
Lists the production exports (gerbers, drill, BOM, placement/CPL)
Includes a first-board bring-up or bench checklist

evals.name: review-latch
evals.prompt: Can you review this soft power latch before I order boards? Tell me anything that's wrong and how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Finds the three planted bugs (floating buck EN, button sense pulled up to VSYS on an MCU GPIO, a 10k latch-gate pull-down that starves the gate) with numbers, and no false alarms.
assertions: Finds that PWR_EN (the buck EN) floats when Q_PWR1 is off and proposes a pull-down
Finds that R_BTN_PU1 pulls PWR_BTN_SENSE (U_MCU1.IO2) up to VSYS, above the ESP32-S3 pin's VDD+0.3 V limit, and moves the pull-up to 3V3
Finds that the 10 kΩ R_LATCH_G1 and 100 kΩ R_INV_PU1 leave the latch gate far below the AO3400A's 0.65 V minimum threshold on a press, so the board can't turn on, and raises R_LATCH_G1 (e.g. to 1 MΩ)
Shows numbers for each finding: node voltages at the supply extremes and datasheet thresholds
Ran stackup check and reports its EN finding
Reports no false defects (e.g. doesn't call the AO3400A, the diode-OR or the inverter wrong)
Any edited design passes stackup check with 0 errors; otherwise the exact changes are given
Recommends or runs a latch simulation after the fixes
Answers in the reply without project scaffolding (no new README, CI or notes files)

evals.name: pin-assign
evals.prompt: Assign the MCU pins for the XBee SPI, the status LED and the three buttons on this board, and wire them up in the design.
evals.expected_output: Pins avoid the N16R8's octal-PSRAM GPIO35-37, strap pins and USB/UART0; the XBee ATTN pull-up resistor is kept; a GPIO table; the design checks clean.
assertions: Assigns nothing to GPIO35-37 (octal PSRAM on the N16R8 module) and says why
Assigns nothing to strap pins IO0, IO3, IO45, IO46, or justifies an exception with its rest level at reset
Leaves USB D+/D- (GPIO19/20) and UART0 (TXD0/RXD0) free, or justifies using them
Wires the XBee SPI lines, SSEL, SPI_ATTN, ON_SLEEP and DTR to MCU pins that support those functions
Keeps the XBee's SPI_ATTN pull-up resistor (the part's default bootmode block) instead of relying on a firmware pull-up
Wires the buttons as active-low inputs and states how they're pulled up
Drives the LED from an MCU pin with its current checked against the pin's drive
Gives a GPIO table: pin, net and reason
The edited design passes stackup check with 0 errors

evals.name: analyzer-claims
evals.prompt: My friend ran an analyzer on my power latch and sent me this report (analyzer-report.txt). Can you fix these issues?
evals.expected_output: Rejects E1 (EN already has a pull-down) and W1 (wrong diode drop and wrong FET threshold), confirms and fixes E2 (button pull-up to VSYS on IO2), and explains each.
assertions: Rejects E1 by showing R_PWR_EN_PD1 already pulls PWR_EN down, and adds no second pull-down
Confirms E2 and fixes it by moving R_BTN_PU1 to 3V3 (or an equivalent that keeps IO2 within its rail), noting the real idle level is VSYS (up to ~4.5 V)
Rejects W1 by re-deriving the gate voltage with the real diode drop at µA (~2.4 V at 3.0 V) against the AO3400A's 1.45 V maximum threshold, pointing out the report's 0.7 V and 2.5 V assumptions
Does not swap Q_LATCH1
Checks the E2 fix doesn't break the inverter (R_INV_BASE1 has its own VSYS pull-up)
The edited design passes stackup check with 0 errors
Explains to the user which claims were wrong and why

evals.name: footprint-check
evals.prompt: Before I send this board to fab, can you check that the footprints match the parts?
evals.expected_output: Flags D1 (5x5 mm PLCC4 footprint for a 3.2x2.8 mm SK6812MINI-E) and D2 (2-pad SOD-123 for a SOT-323 BAT54W-7-F) from manufacturer drawings; confirms Q1 and R1.
assertions: Measures the footprints on the board (footprint_geometry.py or equivalent), not just their names
Flags D1: the 5.0 x 5.0 mm PLCC4 footprint doesn't fit the SK6812MINI-E's 3.2 x 2.8 mm reverse-mount body
Flags D2: a 2-pad SOD-123 footprint for BAT54W-7-F, which is a 3-pin SOT-323 part
Confirms Q1 (SOT-23, AO3400A) and R1 (0402) match their parts
Takes the part dimensions from the manufacturers' datasheets and cites them
Proposes correct footprints, noting the reverse-mount LED needs a board cutout
Leaves the original board file unmodified unless it says what it changed

evals.name: bom-export
evals.prompt: Export the BOM for JLCPCB assembly and make sure it's complete.
evals.expected_output: Every line has manufacturer, MPN, LCSC and an unambiguous package; the BAT54W footprint/package mismatch and the connector orientation are caught even though the checker doesn't flag them.
assertions: Exports with stackup bom (--locked) and checks it with bom_check.py or equivalent
Adds a verified LCSC number for R1
Gives C1 a specific part: manufacturer, MPN, voltage rating, dielectric and LCSC
Removes the comma from Q1's value
Catches that D1's library-default MPN BAT54W-7-F is SOT-323 while its footprint is SOD-123, and resolves it
Adds the right-angle orientation to J1's value or description
The final design passes stackup check and bom_check --fab jlc with 0 problems
Delivers the BOM CSV

evals.name: quick-question
evals.prompt: Quick question: is 10k plus 1µF on the ESP32-S3's EN pin OK?
evals.expected_output: A short yes with the ~10 ms time constant and Espressif's recommendation, and no files.
assertions: Answers yes and gives the RC time constant (about 10 ms)
Cites Espressif's datasheet or hardware design guidelines for the EN (CHIP_PU) RC
Explains why the delay matters (EN must rise after the supply is stable)
Writes no files besides response.md
Stays short: under about 300 words and at most 8 tool calls

evals.name: part-substitute
evals.prompt: The AO3401A for Q_PWR1 is out of stock at JLC this week. What can I use instead? Same footprint please.
evals.expected_output: A pin-compatible SOT-23 P-FET checked against this circuit (threshold vs the gate drive at 3.0 V, Rds(on) at low Vgs, Vds), with tier and stock, the placement updated, and no unnecessary simulation.
assertions: Looks up candidates' JLCPCB tier and stock, several parts per call
Confirms the candidate's SOT-23 pinout (G1 S2 D3) from the manufacturer's drawing
Checks the candidate against the circuit: |Vgs(th)| max below the gate drive at VSYS 3.0 V, Rds(on) specified at |Vgs| of 2.5 V or less, and Vds rating well above 4.5 V
Checks the off state (R_GATE1 holds the gate at VSYS) against the candidate's leakage
Updates Q_PWR1 with manufacturer, MPN and LCSC, and stackup check passes with 0 errors
Doesn't run a new simulation unless the part's thresholds or pinout differ materially, or says why it did
Names a second source
